clue.text: Female getting nothing in early part of year

indicators.note: the month is said to get something, taking it inside itself

parts.note: January, the year's first month, abbreviated
zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman receives nothing at the start of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: JAN takes O in its middle to give JOAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan is a woman's given name, so any female so called fits the general label.

clue.text: In first-class coaches, a hundred can be accommodated, they calculated

parts.note: A is the top grade, as in A1

indicators.note: things accommodated are housed inside something else, here the vehicles

parts.note: A as written, C the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: First-class coaches have room for a hundred passengers, someone reckoned.
explanation.walkthrough: The hundred sits just inside the coaches, after their first letter, not in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Abacuses are bead frames used for counting, devices that once did people's arithmetic, so 'they calculated' describes them.

clue.text: Reptile atop American flower

explanation.surface: A crocodile perched on top of an American bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'atop' puts CROC above US.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small spring-flowering bulb plant, an example of a flower.

clue.text: Supporting family, summon up a kind of energy

indicators.note: in a down answer, going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite someone is to summon them to court

explanation.surface: Backing your relatives, you muster some sort of energy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece 'supporting' another sits beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic energy is the energy a body possesses because of its motion, one recognised type of energy.

clue.text: This lady has a rare article printed by weekly magazine

parts.note: R is a dictionary abbreviation for rare
Bella is a British women's weekly magazine

explanation.surface: A woman has an unusual piece published in a weekly magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Bella is a UK women's weekly; 'printed by' puts ARA beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabella is a female given name, so this particular lady is called that.

clue.text: Accordingly one gets to Romanian capital earlier

indicators.note: a capital is the head or top letter of a word, so only its opening letter counts

explanation.surface: Consequently someone reaches Bucharest ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Romanian capital' looks like Bucharest but means the first letter of Romanian.
explanation.definitionFit: Sooner is the comparative of soon, meaning at an earlier time than another.

clue.text: Leader of Socialists wants beard cut

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

parts.note: an awn is the bristly beard on an ear of barley or other grass

explanation.surface: A left-wing party chief wants a beard trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: The beard here is botanical: AWN, the bristles on a grain ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawn is the past participle of saw, describing wood or similar that has been cut through.

clue.text: Wearing a kind of jacket, I briefly drag back officer

indicators.note: the jacket is worn around the letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a bomber jacket is a short zipped flying jacket

indicators.note: going back means the letters are read from right to left
briefly means made shorter, so the word loses its end

explanation.surface: Pulling on a jacket, I quickly haul an officer back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' joins the shortened word before the turn, so both are read backwards together.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombardier is a non-commissioned rank in the British artillery, so such a person is an officer of sorts.

clue.text: Every other character in pool half Norwegian

indicators.note: every other character means taking alternate letters and skipping the rest

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of each word

explanation.surface: Half of every pool user is a Norwegian swimmer, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the even letters of 'pool half' gives OLAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Olaf is a common Scandinavian man's name borne by several kings of Norway, so it stands for a Norwegian person.

clue.text: Dad's brother maybe reserves really cool transport for the circus?

indicators.note: to reserve something is to keep it held within

parts.note: a father's brother is an uncle; 'maybe' as a mother's brother is one too

explanation.surface: An uncle keeps a very cool vehicle for performing in the big top.
explanation.walkthrough: UNCLE holds ICY: UN(ICY)CLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-wheeled cycle is a classic prop of clowns and acrobats, hence a ride for circus acts.

clue.text: Nuts running short? Here's fresh fruit

indicators.note: running short means the word falls a letter short at its end

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: We've run out of nuts, so here is some fresh fruit instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' looks like food, but it means mad: BANANAS, which loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long curved tropical fruit with a yellow skin, an example of fruit.

clue.text: Examines suspect? That's initially fraught with dangers

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter only

explanation.surface: A police officer searches a suspect, a job full of danger from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To frisk someone is to search them by running hands over their clothing, as police do to suspects.

clue.text: Libertine near northern French city

parts.note: a roué is a debauched man, a rake

explanation.surface: A rake lives close to a city in northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern' seems to describe the city, but it supplies N.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouen is the historic capital of Normandy on the Seine, a city in France.

clue.text: Show cruelty towards a little rogue? That's about right

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters surround another
rogue as an adjective means wayward, out of control, so the letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Being nasty to a small rascal, which seems fair enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little rogue' looks like a small scamp; really the two words 'a little' are rearranged and wrapped around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To ill-treat is to treat badly or abuse, which is acting cruelly towards someone.

clue.text: Former Russian cooperative later disbanded

indicators.note: a disbanded group is broken up and scattered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Soviet-era collective was later broken up.
explanation.walkthrough: An artel is a word solvers meet mostly in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: An artel was a workers' association or collective in Russia, an old form of cooperative enterprise.

clue.text: Doctor's recalled drug after flu outbreak's exaggerated

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards
an outbreak bursts the word apart so its letters come out in a new order

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, plus the S of the possessive
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A GP's withdrawn medicine after an influenza epidemic is said to be overblown.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 's means 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome praise is excessive or overdone, laid on too thick, so fulsome means exaggerated.

clue.text: Orchestra leader accompanies various mates so majestically

indicators.note: various means diverse, mixed, so the letters come in a different order
the leader of a word is the letter at its front

explanation.surface: The leader of the orchestra joins a group of friends playing grandly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestra leader' sounds like the first violinist but gives just O, which follows the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Maestoso is the Italian musical direction to play in a stately, dignified manner.

clue.text: A bishop takes sauna maybe on special rest day

indicators.note: one thing placed on another follows it, so the abbreviation here comes first with the rest built on it

parts.note: a sauna is one kind of bath

explanation.surface: A clergyman enjoys a steam bath on a special day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On special' puts the S in front of A, B and BATH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day set aside for religious observance and rest from work.

clue.text: Old boy upset in home surprisingly shows geniality

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down answer the letters are flipped

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for a former pupil

indicators.note: surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A former pupil, distressed at home, unexpectedly displays good cheer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonhomie is friendly good nature and cheerful companionability, the same quality as geniality.

clue.text: Lifted head before kick-off: new infringement of rugby rules

indicators.note: lifted means raised, so in a down answer the word is read upwards

parts.note: conk is British slang for the head or nose
KO is the abbreviation for kick-off in football fixtures

explanation.surface: A player raised his head before the start of play, a new breach of the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kick-off' looks like the first letter of kick but is the fixture-list abbreviation KO.
explanation.definitionFit: A knock-on is the rugby offence of knocking the ball forward with hand or arm, breaking a rule of play.

clue.text: You'll see TV programme here about tin Indian's preserved

indicators.note: something preserved is kept safely inside, as in a tin

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
the Cree are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A TV show about a tinned curry is being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Indian stands for 'is': the Indian is preserved in the tin.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on-screen appears on the television display, which is where you watch a programme.

clue.text: Singing exam: child's top

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: A singing test: the child comes first.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'top' places the child's abbreviation above the exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral is an adjective for music performed by a choir, so choral works are singing ones.

clue.text: Academic, say, returns holding large computer accessory

parts.note: a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the other way
holding means keeping another letter inside

parts.note: standard abbreviation, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: A lecturer comes back carrying a big computer gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'say' returns; the academic stays as he is in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A dongle is a small plug-in device for a computer port, providing a wireless link or a software licence.

clue.text: Daughter uses a cover as tablecloth

definitions.note: damask is the fabric, a tablecloth one use of it

explanation.surface: A girl drapes a cover over the table as a cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Damask is a reversible patterned fabric of linen, classically used for fine table linen such as tablecloths.

clue.text: Prefer not to participate in work with solicitor

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
a tout solicits custom, e.g. selling tickets

explanation.surface: Someone would rather stay out of a job alongside a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it is one who solicits trade: a TOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part in a scheme or activity, declining involvement.

clue.text: Amateur's oppo has post for support

parts.note: a professional is the opposite of an amateur
P is short for post, as in p&p

explanation.surface: A professional sportsman takes a post for something to lean on.
explanation.walkthrough: Oppo is British slang for a mate or counterpart; here it plays on 'opposite'.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a pole or beam holding something up, a physical support.

clue.text: Rogue containing riotous mob, one reaching a land out east

indicators.note: containing means holding the other letters inside
riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: A scoundrel inside an unruly crowd, one person making it to some far eastern country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes the rogue sit inside the mob; in the wordplay it is the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a country in Southeast Asia, a nation in the Far East.

clue.text: Yogi ceremoniously carries cake decorator

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, spanning the join

explanation.surface: A yogi solemnly bears someone who ices cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An icer is a person who spreads icing on cakes, decorating them.

clue.text: I'm a star in old Bristol area, making comeback

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Avon was an English county, abolished in 1996, that included Bristol

explanation.surface: A celebrity from old Bristol announces a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer itself, a first-person clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness, so it can say it is a star.

clue.text: Like this, article in store is sold off with hope?

definitions.note: describes the article: the answer is an adjective

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A damaged item in a shop is sold cheaply in the hope of clearing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a description of such an article, which is marked down to shift it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop-soiled goods are slightly damaged or faded from being on display, typical of an item in store.
